correctness.rationale: TARGET route: upper bound and Koksma lemma verify, but headline lower bound is unproved. Lemma 1 congruence proof, Weil+Erdos-Turan upper D_p<<log p/sqrt(p), Remark on p=3 mod 4 avoiding atom at 0, and Lemma 2 D_p>=|K(1,1;p)|/2pi(p-1) were checked line-by-line and reproduced numerically (1105 pairs pass; Koksma holds for p=3 mod 4 <=200). Lemma 3 claims Katz vertical Sato-Tate over p=3 mod 4 gives equidistribution of theta_p for diagonal K(1,1;p) and hence infinitely many |K|>=sqrt(p). Cited Katz Ch.9 and Fouvry-Kowalski-Michel Duke 2014 do not prove diagonal equidistribution as modulus varies in a progression; they give horizontal equidistribution (vary a, fixed p) and power-saving for sums over primes of fixed-modulus trace functions. Diagonal vertical Sato-Tate as p varies is not an established black box. Hence infinitely-often lower bound and two-sided headline remain unproved.

originality.rationale: Fused search plus full fetches of nearest priors shows no prior states or implies the fixed-prime two-sided D_p rate for p=3 mod 4 with infinitely-often c/sqrt(p)log p lower bound. Nearest works are Vardi/Myerson averaged equidistribution, Banks-Shparlinski general-set uniformity arXiv:1411.1820, Jun-Lee averaged equidistribution arXiv:1303.2331, Katz horizontal Sato-Tate, FKM fixed-modulus sums over primes, and Dunn-Zaharescu fixed-modulus sums in progression. Upper rate alone is a standard Weil+Erdos-Turan corollary acknowledged in Banks-Shparlinski comments, but the conjunction with the diagonal large-value lower bound is not recorded, mechanically implied, or covered as a special case.

value.rationale: If true, the two-sided fixed-ensemble discrepancy rate for the natural object {{12s(h,p)}} over full reduced residues at primes 3 mod 4 would be independently retrievable: object and invariant were motivated before computation by Rademacher, Vardi, Myerson and Banks-Shparlinski programs, the infinitely-often 1/sqrt(p) scale lower bound is not known or mechanically implied, and a future researcher could reasonably need the precise rate. This is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration.
